ops.text:
I released v0.36.0 and opened #362 with the remaining pi-action changes. #362 is open for your review; I didn't merge it because turning on `trust_project` is a security decision.

**Action pins:** pi-action was already upgraded to v2.4.0 on `main` (commit 70f1a86). The other pins are already on their latest releases, and each pinned commit matches its tag: `actions/checkout` v7.0.1, `actions/setup-node` v7.1.0, `actions/dependency-review-action` v5.0.0 and `actions/create-github-app-token` v3.3.0. There was nothing else to bump.

**Release v0.36.0** ([release page](https://github.com/cv/pit/releases/tag/v0.36.0))
- The release PR (#361) passed CI and was rebase-merged as `adda0a0`. CI also passed on that `main` commit. I then pushed the `v0.36.0` tag on it, and the Release workflow published the release.
- The main change: on pi-action and other pi-durable hosts, Pit now hides the built-in coding tools (`read`, `write`, `edit`, `bash`, `powershell`) from the model. That changes what the model sees in existing pi-action workflows, so I made it a minor release rather than a patch.
- I checked the release targets the tagged commit and has no assets. A fresh clone of the tag installs its dependencies and runs the sandbox.
- Before tagging, all the local checks in `docs/releasing.md` passed, including all 1827 tests.
- I didn't do the interactive install-and-reload smoke test from `docs/releasing.md`; this runner has no interactive Pi session.

**#362, ready to merge** (CI passed). It changes `.github/workflows/pi-assistant.yml`:
- **pit v0.35.1 → v0.36.0.**
- **`trust_project: true`.** `AGENTS.md` tells pi to use `delivery.validate()`, `delivery.prepare()` and the rest of `.pi/functions`, but none of them load in CI today (this run had none). This setting makes pi load them, and also `.pi/pit.json`. I think it's safe here:
  - only owners and members can start a run;
  - comment-triggered runs check out `main`;
  - pull requests from forks get no secrets, so they can't get the App token.
- **`
